videos.headline: The microwave Short reached 45 views and lost almost everyone after the hook: only 4.2% held after it.

why.text: 45 views, against 118 and 255 for the channel's two later Shorts.
26.8% viewed of 60 s; 4.2% held after the hook, on 37 Analytics views.
The steepest fall was 34.8 points at 7.5 s (the line isn't known: the stats job looked for this channel's timeline in the wrong folder, fixed tonight).
97.3% of views came from the Shorts feed, all from the US.

videos.next: Reach the surprising invention moment before 7 s and cut the Short well under 60 s: by 7.5 s only 43.5% of the starting viewers were left.

videos.headline: The Hoover Dam Short reached 118 views, above the channel's small median, but lost viewers at the first big figure.

why.text: 118 views at about 48 hours, against the channel's median of 82 (only 2 Shorts with a 48-hour count).
47.4% stayed to watch (median 53.7%) and 14.8% held after the hook (median 12.8%) across 60 s.
The steepest fall, 18.5 points, came at 7.5 s on 'Historically, it made up to 2,074 megawatts. So how does water make power?'.

videos.next: Put a figure viewers can feel (homes powered, not megawatts) in the first 8 s: the megawatt line is where 18.5 points left.

videos.headline: The first-transistor Short is the channel's best yet: 287 views in two days and a quarter of viewers held after the hook, but a quarter left when the question was asked again.

why.text: 287 views at about 48 hours, against the channel's median of 118 (3 Shorts).
56.5% viewed against a median of 46.3%; 25.6% held after the hook against a median of 13.1%.
The steepest fall, 24.5 points, came at 6.2 s on 'The transistor. What did the very first one look like?', a second asking of the hook's question.

videos.next: Ask the question once, in the hook, and go straight to the first answer picture in the second line: the repeat question is where 24.5 points left.

videos.headline: Crossrail is the channel's breakout: 1,405 views, and viewers watched almost all of it (95% viewed).

why.text: 1,405 views so far against the channel's median of 117 (3 earlier Shorts); 98% came from the Shorts feed.
95% viewed against a median of 46%; 46.5% held after the hook against 13.1%; 58.9% stayed to watch against 56.9%.
The steepest fall, 15.4 points, came at 5.6 s on 'How? Its machines were 150 metres long', where the question is asked again before the answer.

videos.next: Keep the one-line conflict hook, but drop the second 'How?' and open beat two straight on the machine.

videos.headline: The brick phone drew 1,407 views in 48 hours, but under half stayed to watch.

why.text: 1,407 views in 48 hours against the Shorts median of 88.
58.3% viewed, on the median of 58.4%, but 46.9% stayed to watch against 58.3%.
18.7 points left at 5.5 s on "Its engineers had just 6 weeks to build one".

videos.next: Answer the hook's question (why a brick) by the second beat instead of a deadline detail.

videos.headline: Paris Metro on rubber tyres is the channel's most watched Short: 1,629 views, 67.2% viewed.

why.text: 1,629 views in 48 hours against the Shorts median of 88.
67.2% viewed against the median of 58.4%; 59% stayed to watch.
22.2 points left at 6.7 s on "Paris first tried it in 1951. So what keeps it on the track?"
97% of views came from the Shorts feed.

videos.next: Show the answer starting (the tyres under the car) on the second beat; a date and a repeated question there lost the most viewers.

videos.headline: Starlink's long video has 7 views, all of its traffic from search so far.

why.text: 7 views; there is no earlier long video on the channel to compare with.
50.3% viewed and 66.7% stayed to watch, on 7 views.
All 3 views with a known source came from YouTube search ("starlink").

videos.next: Too few long videos to judge; keep the searchable product name at the front of the title.
